newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 20.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday:

* On Wednesdasy, the Dow Jones industrial average ended 47.33 points lower at 7,020.13, one day after racing to an all-time high of 7,067.46 as investors took profits after news that inflation was still in check in January gave the market a brief boost.

* The death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping late on Wednesday is likely to have small affect on overall market sentiment with analysts believing his death will probably have little effect on the functioning of the country.
* Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad told parliament on Tuesday the Indonesian government's outstanding foreign debt stood at $54.6 billion on November 30, 1996.
MARKET
* On Wednesday, the Jakarta Composite Index closed 0.33 points lower, or 0.05 percent, at 694.88 points on profit taking in some blue-chips.
* On Thursday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,386.50/7.50 in early trading against the opening of 2,389.50/90.00.
STOCKS TO WATCH
* Spring producer PT Indospring on intense market talk that a founder shareholder was planning to increase its stake in the company.
* Engineering firm PT Bukaka Teknik following a World Bank denial that the bank had awarded the company some world bank-funded projects in East Asian countries.
* Pharmaceutical firm Tempo Scan Pacific following its announcement on Thursday that it had obtained $105 million loan facility from overseas banks.

* Bank Negara Indonesia on a newspaper report that bad-debt in all state-controlled banks had decreased to 7.1 trillion rupiah in November 1996 from 7.9 trillion rupiah in 1995. Total bad-debt for all banks in Indonesia was 10.4 trillion rupiah in November 1996, the report said.

* Telecommunications firm PT Telkom on media reports that its subsidiary cellular phone operator PT Komselindo was planning to offer 25 percent of its stake to foreign investors. The plan was scheduled to be finalised this year.
Also on media reports that Telkom had appointed PT Pasifik Satelit Nusantara to supply 5,000 small satellite terminals (VSAT) to help the company boost its network in remote areas.

* State-controlled tin miner Tambang Timah on Tuesday's government announcement that state companies would be allowed to participate in the huge Busang gold project when it enters the production stage.
* The country's largest car maker Astra International after shareholders approved on Wednesday a new board of commissioners.

* Lippo Life on a report in the Bisnis Indonesia newspaper that the capital market supervisory agency Bapepam had rejected the company's proposal for a rights issue because it was not in line with its prospectus.
* Indonesian salt producer PT Fiskaragung Perkasa on its announcement that the firm had revised up its 1997 net profit forecast to 144 billion rupiah from 104.1 billion rupiah.
* Alumunium products maker PT Prima Alloy Steel on its proposed stock split and bonus share issue at its extraordinary shareholders meeting on March 27.
